modules.title: 同一个页面问题，状态码指出该检查哪一侧
状态码怎样帮助判断该改哪里

items.title: 先读分类，再读数字
items.text: 首位数字分组说明响应类别：2xx 成功类、3xx 重定向、4xx 客户端错误类、5xx 服务器错误类。它帮助决定先看哪里，仍需结合请求与日志定位原因。

items.title: 数字进一步说明原因
items.text: 404 是未找到目标资源的响应，401 表示请求缺少有效认证凭据，400 表示请求内容有问题；具体原因要结合 URL、请求和响应检查。

items.title: 去哪里看
items.text: 浏览器开发者工具的 Network 面板记录每次请求的状态码；接口调试工具和 AI 返回的报错里也会直接给出数字。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 状态码说明这次请求的结果，不说明代码有没有 bug。返回 200 也不代表业务正确，例如保存接口成功返回但内容没有写入，仍要按业务结果验收。

lessonPractice.title: 提交表单后页面提示“网络错误”，Network 面板显示这次请求返回 500。第一步该做什么？

options.label: 按 500 判断问题在服务器一侧，去查服务端日志里的这次请求
options.feedback: 500 是服务端错误类响应。先用请求 ID 在服务日志里关联这次请求；状态码本身还不能定位具体根因。页面提示文字也不能替代这条证据。

options.label: 按页面提示连续重试，重试成功就说明只是偶发抖动
options.feedback: 500 表示响应方报告了服务器侧错误；是否进入你的应用代码、根因在哪里，还要检查关联日志，重试可能掩盖线索。

options.label: 先检查前端代码，因为页面提示是前端显示的
options.feedback: 提示文字由前端决定显示什么，不代表问题出在前端；500 是服务器错误类响应，接下来应结合请求记录查日志。

en.title: A form shows a generic network error, and the Network panel reports 500. What should happen first?

options.label: Treat 500 as a server-side failure and check server logs for this request
options.feedback: 500 is a server-error-class response. Correlate its request ID with server logs; the status alone does not locate the root cause. Page text cannot replace that evidence.

options.label: Retry repeatedly because the page message says network error
options.feedback: 500 means the responding side reported a server error; check correlated logs to see whether the request reached your application and what failed. Retrying can hide clues.

options.label: Inspect frontend code first because the page renders the message
options.feedback: The page decides what text to show; a 500 is a server-error-class response, so check the correlated request in server logs next.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 页面打开返回 404，提交表单返回 500。请在 Network 面板核对请求 URL、状态码和响应内容；再结合路由/部署检查 404，并用请求 ID 查服务日志定位 500。修复后重新请求，并确认页面展示和保存结果都符合预期。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: The page returns 404 and the form returns 500. Check each URL, status, and response in Network; review the route or deployment for the 404, and correlate the 500 request ID with server logs. After fixing it, resend and verify the page and saved data.

learning.assumes: You have seen a page fail to open, an error, or a form that does nothing.
learning.outcome: You can read what a status code category means and decide whether to check the frontend, the deployment, the request, or the server.

modules.title: The same page problem, with the status code pointing to which side to check
How status codes guide where to look

items.title: Read the category first
items.text: The first digit groups response classes: 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, and 5xx server error. This guides the next check; use the request and logs to locate a cause.

items.title: The exact number narrows the cause
items.text: A 404 response says the target resource was not found, 401 means valid authentication credentials are missing, and 400 signals a problem with the request. Check the URL, request, and response for the cause.

items.title: Where to find it
items.text: The browser Network panel records the status code of every request; debugging tools and errors reported by AI agents also print the number directly.

modules.title: What it does not tell you
modules.text: A status code describes the request outcome, not whether the code has bugs. A 200 also does not prove the business result: a save endpoint can return success while nothing was written, so acceptance still depends on the business outcome.

distinctions.label: On-page error text
distinctions.text: Text like loading failed is decided by frontend code and may appear regardless of the response. The status code comes from the server and is the more reliable first piece of evidence.

distinctions.label: HTTP method
distinctions.text: The method says what the request intends to do; the status code says what the response reported. A resource can return 405 when a method is disallowed, but a wrong method can also produce another response.
